hints: Focus on what dehydration of an alcohol does, it removes water to form a C=C double bond, and each different place you can remove H can give a different structural alkene.
Notice that an alkene like pent-2-ene can exist as two stereoisomers, E and Z, so one structural product can count as two organic products.
Test pentan-3-ol for symmetry, both sides of the C-OH give the same pent-2-ene skeleton, so you only get the E/Z pair.
walkthrough:
**Recall dehydration rule**

Alcohols dehydrate with hot concentrated phosphoric(V) acid by losing OH from the C-OH carbon and H from an adjacent carbon.

$$\text{R-CH(OH)-CH} \rightarrow \text{R-C=C} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Analyse option A, pentan-3-ol**

X is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The C-OH is C3, neighbours are C2 and C4, both $\text{CH}_2$ groups in identical ethyl environments.

Removing H from either side gives the same skeleton, pent-2-ene:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Count stereoisomers**

Pent-2-ene has different groups on each end of C=C, so it shows E/Z (geometric) isomerism. That gives exactly two organic products, (E)-pent-2-ene and (Z)-pent-2-ene. This matches the question.

**Check why others give more than two**

Pentan-2-ol gives pent-1-ene plus E and Z pent-2-ene, total 3. The tertiary alcohol in C gives a terminal alkene plus E and Z of a substituted pent-2-ene, total 3. The diol in D can dehydrate in more ways. Only A gives exactly two.

options.A: Pentan-3-ol is symmetrical about C3. Loss of water to either side gives only pent-2-ene as the structural product, but pent-2-ene exists as E and Z stereoisomers. Total = 2 organic products, exactly as required.
options.B: Pentan-2-ol, CH3CH2CH2CH(OH)CH3, is unsymmetrical. Loss of H from C1 gives pent-1-ene (1 product) and loss from C3 gives pent-2-ene which splits into E and Z (2 products). Total = 3 products, too many.
options.C: 3-methylpentan-3-ol is tertiary with two types of adjacent H. Loss from the methyl group gives 3-methylenepentane (1 product) and loss from an ethyl group gives 3-methylpent-2-ene which splits into E and Z (2 products). Total = 3 products, too many.
options.D: Pentane-2,3-diol has two OH groups and can lose water in several different positions to give different unsaturated alcohols, dienes or carbonyl compounds by rearrangement. It will give more than two organic products, not exactly the E/Z pair.
